title: Mum tidies up
setting: Saturday morning at Yuki's small flat in the city. Her mum has come to stay for the weekend, and two bags of rubbish are sitting by the front door. Partway through, Yuki heads out to the shops and comes back an hour later.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: okaasan, douzo. gomen ne, heya chirakatteru kedo.
lines.ja: お母さん、どうぞ。ごめんね、部屋散らかってるけど。
lines.kana: おかあさん、どうぞ。ごめんね、へやちらかってるけど。
lines.english: Come on in, Mum. Sorry, the place is a mess.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kono heya, itsu kite mo chirakatteru wa ne. kore, nani? gomi?
lines.ja: この部屋、いつ来ても散らかってるわね。これ、何？ゴミ？
lines.kana: このへや、いつきてもちらかってるわね。これ、なに？ごみ？
lines.english: This room's a mess every time I come. And what's this? Rubbish?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un. kinou wa asa ga hayakute, gomi dasu no wasurechatta.
lines.ja: うん。昨日は朝が早くて、ゴミ出すの忘れちゃった。
lines.kana: うん。きのうはあさがはやくて、ごみだすのわすれちゃった。
lines.english: Yeah. I had an early start yesterday and forgot to put the rubbish out.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mou. shigoto ga isogashii no wa wakaru kedo, heya gurai katazukenasai.
lines.ja: もう。仕事が忙しいのはわかるけど、部屋ぐらい片付けなさい。
lines.kana: もう。しごとがいそがしいのはわかるけど、へやぐらいかたづけなさい。
lines.english: Honestly. I know work's busy, but you could at least tidy your room.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: wakatteru yo. demo, kitanaku wa nai desho? chotto chirakatteru dake.
lines.ja: わかってるよ。でも、汚くはないでしょ？ちょっと散らかってるだけ。
lines.kana: わかってるよ。でも、きたなくはないでしょ？ちょっとちらかってるだけ。
lines.english: I know. But it's not dirty, is it? It's just a bit messy.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: tsukatta mono o moto ni modosanai kara, chirakaru no yo.
lines.ja: 使ったものを元に戻さないから、散らかるのよ。
lines.kana: つかったものをもとにもどさないから、ちらかるのよ。
lines.english: You never put things back after you use them. That's why it gets messy.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai hai. kaimono ni itte kitara, heya katazukeru kara.
lines.ja: はいはい。買い物に行ってきたら、部屋片付けるから。
lines.kana: はいはい。かいものにいってきたら、へやかたづけるから。
lines.english: Yeah, yeah. I'll tidy my room when I get back from the shops.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ii wa yo. watashi ga katazuketoku kara, itte kinasai.
lines.ja: いいわよ。私が片付けとくから、行ってきなさい。
lines.kana: いいわよ。わたしがかたづけとくから、いってきなさい。
lines.english: Don't worry, I'll tidy up while you're out. Off you go.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: honto? jaa, gomi wa sutete ii kedo, hoka no mono wa sutenaide ne. itte kuru!
lines.ja: ほんと？じゃあ、ゴミは捨てていいけど、ほかのものは捨てないでね。行ってくる！
lines.kana: ほんと？じゃあ、ごみはすてていいけど、ほかのものはすてないでね。いってくる！
lines.english: Really? Then you can throw away the rubbish, but don't throw out anything else, OK? See you in a bit!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tadaima! e, sugoi! heya, katazuketa dake ja nakute, souji mo shita no?
lines.ja: ただいま！え、すごい！部屋、片付けただけじゃなくて、掃除もしたの？
lines.kana: ただいま！え、すごい！へや、かたづけただけじゃなくて、そうじもしたの？
lines.english: I'm home! Wow, amazing! You didn't just tidy the room, you cleaned it too?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou yo. gomi wa zenbu sutete, fuku mo hon mo moto ni modoshita wa.
lines.ja: そうよ。ゴミは全部捨てて、服も本も元に戻したわ。
lines.kana: そうよ。ごみはぜんぶすてて、ふくもほんももとにもどしたわ。
lines.english: That's right. I threw all the rubbish away, and put your clothes and books back where they go.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: arigatou! are? koko ni atta gomi wa?
lines.ja: ありがとう！あれ？ここにあったゴミは？
lines.kana: ありがとう！あれ？ここにあったごみは？
lines.english: Thank you! Huh? Where's the rubbish that was here?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: aa, ano gomi nara, dashitoita wa yo.
lines.ja: ああ、あのゴミなら、出しといたわよ。
lines.kana: ああ、あのごみなら、だしといたわよ。
lines.english: Oh, that rubbish? I put it out for collection.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, gomi dashichatta no? kyou, doyoubi da yo!
lines.ja: え、ゴミ出しちゃったの？今日、土曜日だよ！
lines.kana: え、ごみだしちゃったの？きょう、どようびだよ！
lines.english: What, you put the rubbish out? It's Saturday today!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: e? datte, gomi wa sutete ii tte itta ja nai.
lines.ja: え？だって、ゴミは捨てていいって言ったじゃない。
lines.kana: え？だって、ごみはすてていいっていったじゃない。
lines.english: What? But you said I could throw the rubbish away.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sore wa heya no gomi no koto! koko wa, gomi wa kayoubi to kin'youbi shika dasenai no.
lines.ja: それは部屋のゴミのこと！ここは、ゴミは火曜日と金曜日しか出せないの。
lines.kana: それはへやのごみのこと！ここは、ごみはかようびときんようびしかだせないの。
lines.english: I meant the rubbish in the room! Round here, rubbish can only go out on Tuesdays and Fridays.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou na no? gomen ne. jaa, sugu totte kuru wa.
lines.ja: そうなの？ごめんね。じゃあ、すぐ取ってくるわ。
lines.kana: そうなの？ごめんね。じゃあ、すぐとってくるわ。
lines.english: Oh, is that so? Sorry. I'll go and get it right away, then.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un. dashita mono wa, moto ni modoshite ne.
lines.ja: うん。出したものは、元に戻してね。
lines.kana: うん。だしたものは、もとにもどしてね。
lines.english: Okay. Whatever you take out, put it back where it was!

choices.english: Mum tidies the flat but throws out some of Yuki's things by mistake, so she has to go and get them back.
Mum tidies the flat and puts the rubbish out, but it isn't a collection day, so she has to go and get it back.
Yuki forgot to put the rubbish out, so Mum puts it out for her on the right day and tidies the flat too.

questions.explanation: In line 8 Mum offers to tidy while Yuki goes shopping, and in line 9 Yuki says she can throw away the rubbish but nothing else. When Yuki gets back (lines 10-11) the room is tidy and clean. But in line 13 Mum says she put the rubbish out (dashitoita), and Yuki points out that it's Saturday (line 14): rubbish only goes out on Tuesdays and Fridays (line 16). In line 17 Mum says she'll go and get it (totte kuru). A is wrong: Mum threw away only the rubbish in the room and put the clothes and books back (line 11). None of Yuki's things were thrown out by mistake. C is wrong: Yuki did forget to put the rubbish out (line 3), but Mum put it out on a Saturday, which is the wrong day.

questions.english: Before she heads out to the shops, Yuki tells Mum what she can do with the rubbish. What did Yuki say?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、買い物に行く前に、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、かいものにいくまえに、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, kaimono ni iku mae ni, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: you can put the rubbish out (for collection), but...
you can toss the rubbish (through the air), but...
you can throw the rubbish away, but...

questions.explanation: Line 9: 'gomi wa sutete ii kedo, hoka no mono wa sutenaide ne' (you can throw away the rubbish, but don't throw out anything else). suteru is getting rid of something. Yuki meant the rubbish lying around the room (line 16: sore wa heya no gomi no koto), and Mum quotes her in line 15. A is wrong: gomi o dasu is putting the bags out for collection. If Yuki had said that, Mum would have been right to put the bags out, and Yuki couldn't complain in lines 14-16. B is wrong: nageru is throwing through the air, like a ball. gomi o nageru means throwing rubbish away only in Hokkaido and Tohoku dialect.

questions.english: Yuki asks where the rubbish by the door has gone, and Mum says, "ano gomi nara, dashitoita wa yo." What had Mum done with it?
questions.ja: お母さんは、ゴミをどうしましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんは、ごみをどうしましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa, gomi o dou shimashita ka?

choices.english: She'd put the bags out at the collection point to be picked up.
She'd gone through the bags and taken out anything that wasn't rubbish.
She'd emptied the bags into the bin in the kitchen.

questions.explanation: Line 13: gomi o dasu is putting rubbish out for collection, and -toita (-te oita) means she did it for Yuki ahead of time. That's why Yuki says 'kyou, doyoubi da yo!' (line 14): here rubbish can only go out on Tuesdays and Fridays (line 16). Yuki uses the same phrase in line 3 for what she forgot to do yesterday. B is wrong: dasu on its own can mean 'take something out', but with gomi it's the collection chore, and Yuki's complaint is about the day, not about anything missing. C is wrong: putting rubbish in a bin is gomi o suteru, which is what Mum did with the rubbish in the room (line 11). The bags by the door went out.

questions.english: Mum calls the evening before a visit: "ashita, sotchi ni iku kedo, heya daijoubu?" Tell her you'll tidy your room tonight.
questions.ja: 明日、そっちに行くけど、部屋大丈夫？
questions.kana: あした、そっちにいくけど、へやだいじょうぶ？
questions.romaji: ashita, sotchi ni iku kedo, heya daijoubu?
questions.answer: Say you'll tidy up tonight with katazukeru: heya katazukeru (o drops in casual speech), or katazuketoku to get it done before she arrives. katazukeru is putting things away; souji suru would be cleaning (vacuuming and wiping).

modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫。今晩、部屋片付けるから。
modelAnswers.english: It's fine. I'll tidy my room tonight.

modelAnswers.romaji: ima chotto chirakatteru kedo, konban katazuketoku ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 今ちょっと散らかってるけど、今晩片付けとくね。
modelAnswers.english: It's a bit of a mess right now, but I'll tidy up tonight.

questions.explanation: Mum's nag in line 4 is 'heya gurai katazukenasai', and Yuki answers 'heya katazukeru kara' (line 7). In line 8 Mum offers 'watashi ga katazuketoku kara', the -toku form for getting it done ahead. In line 10 Yuki sets katazukeru (putting things away) against souji (cleaning): 'katazuketa dake ja nakute, souji mo shita no?'. A messy room needs katazukeru; souji suru is for a dirty one. You're talking to your mum, so casual is right.

questions.english: Yuki calls you: "ima kara, sotchi ni asobi ni itte mo ii?" Say yes, but warn her that your place is a mess.
questions.ja: 今から、そっちに遊びに行ってもいい？
questions.kana: いまから、そっちにあそびにいってもいい？
questions.romaji: ima kara, sotchi ni asobi ni itte mo ii?
questions.answer: Say yes and warn her with the state form chirakatteru: heya chirakatteru kedo (ga drops in casual speech). Don't say kitanai, which says it's dirty.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii yo! demo, heya chirakatteru kedo, gomen ne.
modelAnswers.ja: いいよ！でも、部屋散らかってるけど、ごめんね。
modelAnswers.english: Sure! My place is a mess, though. Sorry.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, kite kite. heya sugoku chirakatteru kedo, ki ni shinaide ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、来て来て。部屋すごく散らかってるけど、気にしないでね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, come over! My place is a real mess, but don't mind it.

questions.explanation: Yuki opens the door to Mum with exactly this host's apology in line 1: 'gomen ne, heya chirakatteru kedo'. Use the -teru form: chirakatteru is the state, with stuff lying everywhere. In line 5 Yuki says her room isn't kitanai (dirty), only chirakatteru (messy). kitanai is blunter and says it's dirty. Yuki asks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: Mum is staying at your place and takes a book off your shelf: "kono hon, chotto yonde mo ii?" Say yes, and ask her to put it back afterwards.
questions.ja: この本、ちょっと読んでもいい？
questions.kana: このほん、ちょっとよんでもいい？
questions.romaji: kono hon, chotto yonde mo ii?
questions.answer: Say yes and ask her to put it back where it was: moto ni modoshite (ne). The putting-back verb is modosu; modoru is something (or someone) going back by itself.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii yo. yondara, moto ni modoshite ne.
modelAnswers.ja: いいよ。読んだら、元に戻してね。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. Put it back when you're done.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, douzo. demo, ato de chanto moto ni modoshite ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、どうぞ。でも、後でちゃんと元に戻してね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, go ahead. But put it back properly afterwards, OK?

questions.explanation: In line 6 Mum says Yuki's room gets messy because she doesn't put things back: 'tsukatta mono o moto ni modosanai kara'. In line 18 Yuki turns it on her: 'dashita mono wa, moto ni modoshite ne' (whatever you take out, put back), since Mum put the rubbish out. Don't say moto ni modotte, which would tell Mum herself to go back. kaeshite (give it back) is for returning something to its owner; here you want the book back on the shelf.

newWords.english: dirty (kitanaku wa nai: it's not dirty)
cleaning: vacuuming, wiping, dusting (souji suru: clean)
take, pick up (totte kuru: go and get)
at least, if nothing else (heya gurai: at least your room)
do ...! (a parent's firm order: katazukenasai, itte kinasai)
